subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evals, and regression next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap: model fit, evals, and regression next steps

Hi Rachel / Tom —

Great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of needs (from call)
- High-throughput customer support summarization across short tickets (avg 80 tokens).
- Strong hallucination controls and factual grounding for order/context fields.
- Tight latency SLOs for peak spikes (p95 < 250ms).

2) Initial model fit & eval notes (from our side)
- Based on the sample prompts you shared, our evals show the new 2.1.x model family improved latency but introduced a small quality regression on entity extraction (precision drop ~4.3% vs baseline 2.0.9).
- We recommend two immediate tracks: a) run a focused A/B on your top 100 prompt set, b) pin the serving model to 2.0.9 for critical routes while we investigate.

3) Attachments & links I shared: benchmark report (high-level), prompt set CSV, and regression diff log. Chloe and Dev are looped for details on evals and security implications.

Next steps / asks: 
- Rachel: can you confirm which route(s) you'd prefer pinned if we take the pin option? (e.g., /support/summarize-v1)
- Tom: can you share a 24‑hour spike window and the sample event id for last week (helps reproduce p95).
- Chloe/Dev: please add quick notes on rollback timeline and whether pinning affects billing/throughput.

I'll follow up with a short mutual action plan (MAP) after we decide the route.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
https://redwood.ai

Attachments: acme_benchmark_report_v2.pdf, acme_prompt_set_v1.csv, regression-diff-20261214.txt

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Lin <tom.lin@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evals, and regression next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our side: 

1) Pinning: we would likely pin only the customer-support route (/support/summarize-v1) initially. That route powers our highest priority SLA customers.
2) A/B: happy to run A/B, but low risk tolerance — what’s the rollback window if we see issues in the first 2 hours?
3) Data/sample: Tom will share the 24-hour spike and a sample event id shortly.

Also, can you confirm whether pinning to 2.0.9 will change cost or throughput capacity on our Dedicated pool? We need to include this in procurement prep.

-Rachel
Sr. Product Manager, Platform
Acme Retail
rachel.kim@acmeretail.com | +1 206-555-0133

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T20:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evals, and regression next steps

Hi Rachel / team —

Quick technical notes from the eval side (pulling from the Drive eval run: https://docs.redwood.ai/evals/run/EV-2026-11-14):
- Baseline (2.0.9): entity extraction F1 = 0.872, p95 latency = 240ms (dedicated cluster config).
- New candidate (2.1.4): entity extraction F1 = 0.835, p95 latency = 180ms.
- Regression diff log attached (regression-diff-20261214.txt) highlights the most common failure modes: truncated system prompts in 3/100 examples and subtle tokenization differences causing mis-split order IDs.

Recommendations: 
- If SLA is highest priority: pin /support/summarize-v1 to model 2.0.9. Pinning is a config change and can be done within 10–15 minutes with no service interruption; it does not change billing rates for Dedicated capacity (same GPU pool).
- Parallel A/B: create a canary route /support/summarize-v1-canary that routes ~5% of traffic to 2.1.4 for live validation. This gives real-world telemetry while keeping 95% on the pinned version.
- If you want faster fix: we can prepare a targeted quantization/decoding tweak and re-run the evals; that path typically adds 2–4 business days.

Dev — any compliance/security notes about pinning?

- Chloe
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@acmeretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: model fit, evals, and regression next steps

Hi all —

Confirming Chloe’s notes on rollout and pinning:
- Pin = route config change only. No infra migration required. We can pin by route or by tenant (your Dedicated namespace).
- Rollback window: immediate. If canary shows regression we can route 100% back to pinned version within ~5 minutes and invalidate stale KV caches if necessary (that can add ~2–3 minutes to full recovery for edge cases).
- Billing: no change to Dedicated hourly commit for pinned vs unpinned models. If you change instance sizing to support higher throughput, that would affect commit but pin itself is a config.
- Security: pinning is a control plane change; we will record the audit log and include the change request ID in our SOC2 audit bundle. No data plane differences.

Next steps I will take after you confirm:
- Implement pin for /support/summarize-v1 (10–15 min maintenance window, non-disruptive).
- Create a canary route at 5% to 2.1.4 and surface A/B telemetry in Console (I’ll add the dashboard link).

Marissa — can you draft the MAP with timelines and owners and I’ll attach the rollback playbook?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Engineering, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai
